args.entity_id: {sql:loreweave_glossary:SELECT entity_id::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1}

why: Restoring an entity twice must not double-restore or corrupt it. THE PREDICATE IS THE SEED'S OWN, verbatim - book_id plus deleted_at IS NOT NULL, which is exactly what this scenario's seed_assert already checks. Two earlier attempts of mine guessed instead: first a table `entities` that does not exist, then entity_snapshot->>'name' when the seed writes cached_name. The seed is the authority on the fixture it creates. The id must come from SQL at all because no tool lists a soft-deleted entity - which is this tool's own blocking finding, D-RESTORE-WITH-NO-WAY-TO-SEE-WHAT-IS-RESTORABLE. book_id is passed EXPLICITLY: chat-service injects it from the ambient book, and a direct MCP call has no such context — the first attempt was refused 'book_id must be a UUID', which is the tool correctly refusing a call the runtime would normally have completed.
